metadata.title: Dare Ogunbowale Set for a Backup Role
metadata.description: Houston Texans running back Dare Ogunbowale did play seven snaps in Week 7 against the Giants, although he failed to show up in the box score with a catch or a carry. With David Montgomery (groin) and Jawhar Jordan (practice squad injured list) sidelined again in Week 9's matchup with the Chargers, the veteran is lined up to be the primary backup behind Woody Marks once again. Ogunbowale isn't likely to get a large role, though, especially since the team added Emari Demercado from waivers as well. He is only the RB69 this week and remains well off the fantasy radar, barring further injuries ahead of him on the depth chart.

metadata.title: Dare Ogunbowale - No touches on offense in OT loss
metadata.description: Ogunbowale didn't record an offensive touch or target in Sunday's 24-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
metadata.analysis: Even with David Montgomery (groin) and Jawhar Jordan (quadriceps) injured and inactive, Ogunbowale played just seven offensive snaps behind Woody Marks' 54. Ogunbowale can continue to be ignored in fantasy football.

metadata.title: Dare Ogunbowale Expected To Be Primary Backup
metadata.description: Houston Texans running back Dare Ogunbowale will be the second running back for Houston this week against the Giants, with both David Montgomery (groin) and Jawhar Jordan (quad) ruled out. The veteran has been active in each of the last three games but has only played one snap, without a carry or a catch. While Woody Marks is expected to handle almost all the work in the backfield, the team is confident in Ogunbowale's ability to succeed as well, according to offensive coordinator Nick Caley. Caley said of Ogunbowale, "We have faith whoever's out there, we have faith that we're going to put them in the best position." Barring an injury to Marks, though, Ogunbowale will probably be only involved a little bit in the team's game plan. He is only the RB57 in RotoBaller's Week 7 rankings, so he can be left on the waiver wire in all but the deepest of leagues.

metadata.title: Dare Ogunbowale Could Have a Role vs. the Jaguars
metadata.description: Houston Texans running back Dare Ogunbowale is set to be the team's primary backup behind Woody Marks in Week 6 after David Montgomery (groin) was ruled out. The 32-year-old veteran played just one snap last week and didn't touch the ball, but he was the only running back besides Marks and Montgomery to get any offensive work at all. Ogunbowale was on the Raiders' practice squad before joining the Texans, but he has yet to have a catch or carry in his two games this season. Ogunbowale could mix in on third downs due to his pass protection and his contributions as a pass-catcher, but he will likely have a very minimal role as Marks carries the load. The Jaguars have also been one of the best defenses in the league against running backs, making Ogunbowale only worth a look in the deepest of formats or in a DFS Showdown format as a punt play. He is RotoBaller's No. 54 RB this week, so he can be left on the waiver wire in most standard-sized leagues.

metadata.title: Dare Ogunbowale - Back with Texans
metadata.description: The Texans signed Ogunbowale off the Raiders' practice squad Tuesday.
metadata.analysis: Ogunbowale signed with the Raiders' practice squad after being trimmed from the team's roster during final cuts. The running back now returns to Houston, where he participated in 129 offensive snaps and 281 special-teams snaps over 17 regular-season games in 2025.

metadata.title: Dare Ogunbowale signs with Texans
metadata.description: The Texans signed RB Dare Ogunbowale from the Raiders' practice squad.
metadata.analysis: Ogunbowale will add depth in the backfield for Houston.

metadata.title: Dare Ogunbowale - Staying in Las Vegas on practice squad
metadata.description: The Raiders signed Ogunbowale to the practice squad Monday.
metadata.analysis: Ogunbowale was unable to beat out Dylan Laube for the Raiders' RB3 role behind Ashton Jeanty (ankle) and Mike Washington, prompting Las Vegas to release Ogunbowale on Sunday. The veteran running back will stay with the organization as a member of the practice squad, and he could be elevated to the active roster for Week 1 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Sept. 13 if Jeanty is ruled out.

metadata.title: Dare Ogunbowale released by Raiders
metadata.description: The Raiders released RB Dare Ogunbowale.
metadata.analysis: Ogunbowale was competing for a depth role in the backfield. He'll seek another opportunity heading into the season.

metadata.title: Dare Ogunbowale - Released by Raiders
metadata.description: Ogunbowale was released by Las Vegas on Sunday, Tom Pelissero of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: After signing with the Raiders earlier in August, Ogunbowale has failed to make the 53-man roster. The veteran running back had been competing for a depth role, but it looks like the Raiders are content to roll with the younger Mike Washington and Dylan Laube as their backfield depth options behind Ashton Jeanty (ankle), even with Jeanty's status for Week 1 still uncertain.

metadata.title: Dare Ogunbowale - Catches on with Las Vegas
metadata.description: Ogunbowale signed a contract with the Raiders on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: After a four-year run in Houston, Ogunbowale will head to Las Vegas and will battle for a backup running back job in training camp and the preseason. The 32-year-old has averaged just 3.4 yards per carry for his career, but he's been serviceable on passing downs and has found a spot on NFL rosters each of the past nine seasons mainly because of his contributions on special teams. In Las Vegas, Ogunbowale looks set to compete with third-year player Dylan Laube and undrafted rookie Roman Hemby for the third spot on the depth chart behind Ashton Jeanty and fourth-round rookie Mike Washington.
